clue.text: Odd characters in photos are said to be pitiable

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters, first, third and fifth, are the ones kept from the word that follows

parts.note: first, third and fifth letters of the word

indicators.note: something said is heard rather than read, so a word's sound stands in for its spelling

parts.note: the letter R is pronounced like the word are

explanation.surface: Someone's holiday snaps are dismissed as a sorry, pitiable lot.
explanation.definitionFit: Poor in the sense of deserving sympathy, as in 'the poor fellow', is a synonym of pitiable.

clue.text: Coat initially put on demure monarch

parts.note: prim means demure, proper
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the standard abbreviation for the Queen

explanation.surface: A modest sovereign has a garment placed on them first thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' looks like a first-letter signal for put, but it belongs to the definition: the first coat of paint.
explanation.definitionFit: A primer is the preparatory layer of paint applied to a surface before the top coats.

clue.text: Severely criticise second strike

parts.note: s is the abbreviation for second
to lam is to beat or thrash

explanation.surface: A critic delivers a second blow by savaging someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To slam a book or play is informal for attacking it harshly in a review.

clue.text: Rising that's trapping one on island, South Seas paradise

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the word is read from the bottom upwards
trapping something means holding it inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: taken as written, then turned round
the Roman numeral for one
I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: Something rising up traps a lone castaway on a tropical island paradise.
explanation.definitionFit: Tahiti, in French Polynesia, is the classic image of a Pacific island idyll.

clue.text: What's excellent about a metal or another

definitions.note: A pronoun defining a noun, fair because the clue's own 'a metal' supplies what 'another' stands for, so it reads as another metal.

indicators.note: about means going around, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: a plum job is an excellent, desirable one
A plus TIN, a metal

explanation.surface: A question of which precious metal is the finest choice.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the words before it: 'another' means another metal, beyond the tin used in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Platinum is a precious metallic element, so it is a metal besides tin.

clue.text: Police raid disrupted magazine

indicators.note: something disrupted is thrown into disorder, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A raid by officers interrupts the production of a magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: A periodical is a publication issued at regular intervals, which is what a magazine is.

clue.text: Way to achieve entrance as backward children, English learners

indicators.note: backward tells us to read the word from its end to its start

parts.note: a brood is a family of young, turned round here
E is the abbreviation for English
L is a learner, from the L-plate on a learner driver's car; two learners give two

explanation.surface: Slow children learning English find a route into a school.
explanation.definitionFit: Ringing a doorbell is how a visitor gets someone to let them in.

clue.text: Mathematical tasks are set up for Dutch scholar

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means lifted so that the letters read upwards

parts.note: sums are arithmetic problems
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tutor sets arithmetic problems for a student from the Netherlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Erasmus of Rotterdam was the leading Dutch humanist scholar of the Renaissance.

clue.text: Having dropped off former PM's article, returned

indicators.note: returned means sent back the way it came, so the string runs backwards

parts.note: Robert Peel was a 19th-century British Prime Minister, with the possessive S
the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone has delivered a former Prime Minister's piece of writing, which then came back.
explanation.definitionFit: Dropped off is an idiom for having fallen asleep.

clue.text: Area following shameful action in 19th-century war zone

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the first word is placed after the second

parts.note: a crime is a disgraceful act
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: Atrocities committed in a region during a Victorian-era conflict.
explanation.definitionFit: The Crimean War of 1853 to 1856 was fought largely on the Crimean peninsula.

clue.text: Keep a man in it, needing to be reformed

indicators.note: reformed means formed again in a new shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Lock up a man who needs to mend his ways.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep something in good order or running is to maintain it, so the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Previously referred to supervisors in a note I'd composed

indicators.note: in places one word inside the other
composed means put together, so the letters are arranged afresh

parts.note: the letters to rearrange
foremen supervise workers

explanation.surface: A memo I wrote mentioned the bosses earlier.
explanation.definitionFit: Aforementioned is a formal word for something mentioned earlier in the same text.

clue.text: Given legal status supporting African country's education

parts.note: being for something is supporting it
Mali, a West African state, with the possessive S
ed is short for education

explanation.surface: An aid project backing schooling in an African nation gets official approval.
explanation.definitionFit: To formalise something is to make it official, as an agreement is made legally binding.

clue.text: Is one crazy? That's what we hear

indicators.note: crazy means disordered, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone hearing things wonders if they are going mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Noise is sound, and sound is exactly what the ear picks up.

clue.text: Cold cut of meat, or game

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
a rib is a cut of beef or pork

explanation.surface: Choosing between a cold joint of meat and playing a game.
explanation.definitionFit: Crib is the usual short name for cribbage, a card game scored with pegs on a board.

clue.text: It helps to know one's place when one returns to work

definitions.text: It helps to know one's place when one returns to work

parts.words: It helps to know one's place when one returns to work
parts.note: surface reading: something that reminds an employee of their status or task on getting back to the job

parts.words: It helps to know one's place when one returns to work
parts.note: setter's reading: the work is a book, and the place is the page reached when the reader picks it up again

explanation.walkthrough: 'work' suggests a job and 'know one's place' a social rank, but the work is a literary one and the place is the page.
explanation.definitionFit: A strip of card or ribbon left between pages marks where the reader stopped reading.

clue.text: Female is clothed in this, possibly

definitions.text: Female is clothed in this, possibly

indicators.note: being clothed in something means being wrapped inside it, so one piece goes within the other
possibly suggests one of several arrangements, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to rearrange
F is the abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: A woman might well be wearing this garment.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: a woman could indeed be dressed in one.
explanation.definitionFit: A shift is a simple straight dress or a loose undergarment worn by women.

clue.text: Essay about current record of events in book group

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word goes around the rest

parts.note: an essay is an attempt, a try
I is the symbol for electric current
a log is a running record, as a ship's log

explanation.surface: A piece of writing about recent history appears in a reading group's book.
explanation.walkthrough: Essay here means an attempt, not a composition.
explanation.definitionFit: A trilogy is a set of three related novels, a group of books.

clue.text: As part of black comedy, turned to ridicule

indicators.note: turned means facing the other way, so the letters are read backwards
as part of means the letters are a section of the words that follow

parts.note: the letters spanning the two words, read backwards

explanation.surface: Dark humour gets used for scorn.
explanation.definitionFit: To mock someone is to make fun of them, a direct synonym of ridicule.

clue.text: With regret, a poet logically has log moved

indicators.note: moved tells us the order is changed; here only one three-letter run shifts to a new spot

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A rational poet sorrowfully shifts a tree trunk.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the LOG in logically moves: lift it out and put it after APO to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something apologetically means doing it in a way that expresses regret or sorrow.

clue.text: Sounded like pigs in old used pen

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old
using a pen on paper is to have inked it

explanation.surface: Pigs grunting inside a disused old sty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pen' suggests a pigsty, but here it is the writing tool.
explanation.definitionFit: An oink is the grunt a pig makes, so oinked means made pig noises.

clue.text: State that's normal as Kansas at heart

indicators.note: at heart means within the core of the words, so the answer sits inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the three words

explanation.surface: One US state is said to be as ordinary as the heartland.
explanation.definitionFit: Alaska is the largest of the fifty United States.

clue.text: Odd man is absurdly appearing in suit

indicators.note: absurdly means nonsensically, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A strange man turns up wearing a ridiculous outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suit' looks like clothing; it is a suit of playing cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Diamonds is one of the four suits in a pack of cards.

clue.text: Benefit from something made from rice

definitions.meaning: first meaning: good or advantage, as in 'for your own good'
second meaning: Japanese fermented rice wine

explanation.surface: Someone profits from a rice product.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means advantage in 'for the sake of' and also names the Japanese rice wine.

clue.text: Ambiguous prophecy, or a non-U thing like this?

indicators.note: non-U means without the letter U, so that letter is taken out

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
the thing being read is a crossword clue

explanation.surface: A cryptic forecast is compared to a crossword clue, possibly lacking in class.
explanation.walkthrough: Non-U is British slang for not upper class, which disguises the instruction to drop U.
explanation.definitionFit: An oracle, as at Delphi, was a prophecy famously open to double meanings.

clue.text: Makers of chains, we hear, for wild cat

indicators.note: we hear means the word is judged by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: links are what chains are made of

explanation.surface: Chains for restraining a wild animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The lynx is a short-tailed wild feline of northern forests.

clue.text: Eliot the writer? Not he

parts.note: surface reading: a question about whether a writer called Eliot is male, as T S Eliot was
setter's reading: the novelist known by this male first name plus Eliot was really a woman, Mary Ann Evans

explanation.walkthrough: The male pen name hid a female author, so the writer named this way was not a he.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the first name of the pseudonym under which Mary Ann Evans wrote Middlemarch.

clue.text: Man on board protecting a wild ox, going by boat

indicators.note: protecting means surrounding and shielding, so one word goes around the others

parts.note: a king is a chess piece, a man on the board
taken as written
a yak is a long-haired Himalayan ox

explanation.surface: A chess king guards a yak while travelling on water.
explanation.definitionFit: Kayaking is travelling in a kayak, a small enclosed paddle boat.
